_comment: Growing-degree-day models, one per bloom site. Kept as data, not code, so
thresholds can be refit against historical bloom records without a deploy.
gddThreshold is the accumulated heat sum (base baseTempC, from seasonStart)
at which first bloom historically occurs. calibrationStatus records how much
to trust that number: 'fitted' means backfit against a published bloom
series, 'first-pass' means a literature estimate that still needs fitting.
The confidence engine reads calibrationStatus, so an unfitted model
publishes at visibly lower confidence rather than silently guessing.

models.name: Kyoto Cherry Blossom
models.calibratedFrom: Osaka/Kyoto full-flowering records; the Kyoto series runs to the 9th century and is the best training set available for any single-species bloom model.
models.notes: Peak bloom typically 5-7 days after first flowering.

models.name: Tidal Basin Cherry Blossom
models.notes: NPS defines peak bloom as 70% of Yoshino blossoms open.

models.name: Antelope Valley Poppy Superbloom
models.notes: Heat sum alone is a poor predictor here — a superbloom needs sustained autumn rainfall, which the rainfall gate checks separately.

models.name: Keukenhof Tulip Bloom
models.notes: Field bloom, not the indoor pavilions.

models.name: Valensole Lavender Bloom
models.notes: Harvest begins mid-bloom, so the visitable window closes before the botanical one.

models.name: Namaqualand Daisy Bloom
models.calibratedFrom: SANParks bloom-season reporting, typically mid-August to mid-September.
models.notes: Southern-hemisphere bloom. Flowers only open in direct sun and face it, so overcast days show almost nothing.

models.name: Hitachi Seaside Nemophila
models.notes: Roughly 4.5 million plants across Miharashi Hill.
